title: Approve vaginal pH modulation for on-demand non-hormonal contraception

concept.text: Enable woman-controlled pregnancy prevention through a non-hormonal vaginal pH-modulating product used around intercourse. Phexxi achieved approval, but its efficacy is substantially below long-acting contraception. Proposed completion test: FDA approval specifically for on-demand pregnancy prevention, based on a phase 3 study measuring cumulative pregnancy incidence over seven menstrual cycles and reviewing local and urinary safety. Test set by: FDA; its review accepted a seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate of 13.7% with a 95% confidence interval of 10.0–17.5%. This was not a Pearl Index below 2. Reported achieved: FDA approved Phexxi on 22 May 2020. Sources given: [FDA Phexxi approval letter](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/208352Orig1s000ltr.pdf) ; [FDA multidisciplinary efficacy and safety review](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/208352Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf).

page.title: First approved contraceptive acting by vaginal pH modulation
page.definition: A nonhormonal vaginal gel applied before intercourse is approved for preventing pregnancy. It keeps the vagina acidic (low pH) when semen is present, which reduces sperm movement. In the approval trial the cumulative pregnancy rate over seven menstrual cycles of typical use was 13.7% (95% confidence interval 10.0–17.5%), which FDA placed in the range of nonoxynol-9 spermicides and below hormonal methods.

goal.need: In 2019, 41.6% of US pregnancies were unintended. FDA identifies nonhormonal contraception as an option for women who cannot tolerate hormones or have contraindications to their use, and identifies potential benefit from on-demand dosing for women with infrequent intercourse.

statements.quote: The Panel recommends additional development of female contraceptive modalities that are delivered to the reproductive tract
statements.context: The recommendation concerns blocking egg or sperm function within the female reproductive tract on demand.

statements.quote: we intend to seek regulatory approval for product labeling stating Phexxi can be used on-demand, immediately before or up to one hour before intercourse.
statements.context: The company's annual report for 2019 describes its intended contraceptive indication.

completion.title: FDA approves a vaginal pH-modulating gel for on-demand prevention of pregnancy.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a new drug application for a vaginal product containing no hormone and no nonoxynol-9, whose labelled mechanism is a lowering of vaginal pH that reduces sperm motility, indicated for prevention of pregnancy in females of reproductive potential as an on-demand method used before each act of intercourse. The approval rests on a trial of seven menstrual cycles of typical use in which the upper limit of the 95% confidence interval of the Kaplan–Meier cumulative pregnancy rate is at most 21%. The first such approval meets the test. The test does not require a lower pregnancy rate than spermicides give.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration: approval letter and prescribing information for NDA 208352 (Phexxi) for the indication and mechanism; the review division's comments at a Type A meeting before the phase 3 trial, recorded in the multidisciplinary review, for the pregnancy-rate bound.
completion.threshold_quote: The proposed point estimate for the 7-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate of 16.5% with a prespecified upper bound of the 95% confidence interval of 21% is acceptable
completion.basis: The test names a first of mechanism, not of contraceptive capability. FDA's review found the pregnancy rate (13.7% over seven cycles; Pearl Index 27.5) in the same range as marketed nonoxynol-9 spermicides, significantly less effective than hormonal methods, and comparable in benefit to other on-demand nonhormonal vaginal contraceptives. The 21% bound is the one FDA accepted before the phase 3 trial, not an Atlas threshold. A self-administered nonhormonal method with first-year typical-use failure below 1% is a separate entry, HLT-32.

milestones.title: A vaginal gel keeps a semen mixture below about pH 5 in a laboratory test.
milestones.criterion: In a laboratory assay that mixes the gel directly with human semen from more than one donor, the mixture stays below about pH 5 at a stated gel:semen ratio. The report states the ratio, the number of donors and the measured pH.
milestones.set_by: Rush-Presbyterian-St. Luke's Medical Center inventors, formulation target and laboratory assay in US patent 6,706,276, claim 1 and Example 10.
milestones.threshold_quote: wherein the composition maintains an acidic vaginal pH of less than about 5 in the presence of semen ejaculated from the male

milestones.title: FDA permits a 14-day vaginal-gel safety study in women to proceed.
milestones.criterion: FDA reviews, under an investigational new drug application for the gel, the protocol of a study of at least 14 days of vaginal use in women and determines that it is safe to proceed, on nonclinical evidence that includes a vaginal irritation study in animals. Submission of the application without a recorded determination is partial.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, regulatory history for IND 64623 reproduced in the NDA 208352 multidisciplinary review.
milestones.threshold_quote: Both study protocols were reviewed and determined to be safe to proceed.

milestones.title: A vaginal gel yields fewer than one forward-moving sperm per microscope field in a postcoital test.
milestones.criterion: In a postcoital test in women protected from pregnancy, midcycle cervical mucus sampled after intercourse with the gel applied beforehand contains, as the mean across women, fewer than one progressively motile (forward-moving) sperm per high-power microscope field, averaged across the fields examined, and the same women exceed that cutoff in a cycle without gel.
milestones.set_by: ACIDFORM postcoital-study investigators; the study-specific cutoff is restated by co-investigator Christine K. Mauck and Kathleen L. Vincent in their 2020 account.
milestones.threshold_quote: the cut-off of less than one PMS/HPF in the later Acidform study

milestones.title: A vaginal gel's seven-cycle pregnancy rate has an upper 95% confidence limit of at most 21%.
milestones.criterion: In a phase 3 trial in women aged 18–35 who use the gel before each act of intercourse, the upper 95% confidence limit of the Kaplan–Meier seven-cycle typical-use cumulative pregnancy rate is ≤21%. Evaluable cycles exclude those with backup contraception, without intercourse, or shorter than 21 or longer than 35 days. The report states the number of women, evaluable cycles and pregnancies.
milestones.set_by: Evofem, Inc., AMPOWER protocol AMP002, registered as NCT03243305, version 4 dated 1 November 2017, sections 9.2 and 9.8.
milestones.threshold_quote: the upper limit of the 95% CI of the cumulative seven-cycle pregnancy rate is less than or equal to 21%.

not_found: Full texts of the 2001 ACIDFORM laboratory study and the 2004 postcoital study could not be accessed.
The 2020 AMPOWER article could not be opened through its publisher or PMC.

results.finding: PHEXXI AMP002 phase 3 trial: 101 on-treatment pregnancies; seven-cycle Kaplan–Meier pregnancy rate upper 95% confidence limit was 17.5%; number of women not stated.
results.detail: The upper confidence limit meets the ≤21% threshold, and participants were aged 18–35. The supplied excerpt does not report the number of women or evaluable cycles, or establish all required cycle exclusions. Approval is recommended, but an approval decision is not recorded.
results.quote:
The Applicant and the FDA statistical reviewer determined that the 7-cycle cumulative 
pregnancy rate was 13.7% with a 95% CI of (10.0%, 17.5%) based on 101 on-treatment 
pregnancies.

results.finding: ACIDFORM in a crossover study of 20 sterilized women reduced the mean progressively motile sperm count to 0.19 when applied 0–30 minutes before intercourse.
results.detail: Midcycle postcoital testing found means below one with ACIDFORM and 17.94 in control cycles. However, the supplied text does not state that counts are per high-power microscope field or averaged across examined fields.
results.quote: ACIDFORM or N-9 product administered 0-30 min precoitus or ACIDFORM given 8-10 h precoitus significantly reduced the mean number of progressively motile sperm compared to control cycles (0.19, 0.07, 0.75 vs. 17.94, respectively, p<.05, Wilcoxon test).

results.finding: PHEXXI in 1183 women had a seven-cycle Kaplan–Meier typical-use pregnancy-rate upper 95% confidence limit of 17.5%.
results.detail: The trial reports 4769 evaluable cycles and 101 pregnancies, ages 18–35, dosing before each intercourse episode, and all required cycle exclusions. The label does not explicitly identify the trial as phase 3.
results.quote:
A total of 101 on-treatment pregnancies occurred in 1183 subjects 
contributing 4769 evaluable natural cycles. The 7-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate was 13.7% (95% 
CI: 10.0%, 17.5%),

results.finding: FDA approved PHEXXI for on-demand contraception; its trial in 1183 women had a seven-cycle pregnancy-rate upper 95% confidence limit of 17.5%.
results.detail: The label records initial U.S. approval in 2020, use before each act of intercourse, and pH lowering with reduced sperm motility. Its listed ingredients contain neither hormones nor nonoxynol-9; the supporting trial uses Kaplan–Meier typical-use analysis.

results.finding: Phexxi vaginal gel: among 1,114 women in the efficacy analysis, the upper 95% confidence limit for seven-cycle typical-use pregnancy was 17.5%.
results.detail: Phase 3 enrolled women aged 18–35 using gel before each intercourse; Kaplan–Meier analysis excluded cycles with backup contraception, no intercourse, or lengths outside 21–35 days. Reports 101 pregnancies and over 24,000 qualifying cycles, although that cycle count appears inconsistent with the seven-cycle design and reported intercourse counts.
results.quote: The seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy percentage was 13.7% [95% confidence interval (CI): 10.0%–17.5%], meeting the prespecified primary endpoint of having the upper bound 95% CI ≤ 21%.

results.finding: Phexxi gel in 1,183 women had a seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate with an upper 95% confidence limit of 17.5%.
results.detail: The report gives 4,769 cycles and 101 pregnancies, ages 18–35, dosing before each intercourse episode, and the required cycle exclusions. The upper limit meets the threshold, but the text does not identify the trial as phase 3 or specify Kaplan–Meier estimation or typical use.
results.quote:
A 
total of 101 on-treatment pregnancies occurred in 1,183 subjects contributing 4,769 cycles. The 
7-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate was 13.7% (95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 10.0%, 17.5%),
